title: Quality control of sequencing reads
instructions:
## Four lines per read

A FASTQ file holds reads in blocks of four lines: `@name`, the bases, `+`, and a quality string where each character encodes a Phred score as `ord(char) - 33`. A score of 20 means a 1% chance the base is wrong.

## Do this

Read the FASTQ from standard input. For every read print `name meanQ keep|drop` with the mean quality to one decimal, keeping reads whose mean is **at least 20**. Then print `kept K of N` and the **GC content of the kept reads** as `GC xx.x%` (G and C bases as a percentage of all bases in the kept reads, one decimal).

initialState.source:
import sys

lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
reads = []
for i in range(0, len(lines), 4):
    name = lines[i][1:]
    bases = lines[i + 1]
    quals = lines[i + 3]
    reads.append((name, bases, quals))

# mean quality per read, keep or drop, then the summary and GC content

hints: mean = sum(ord(c) - 33 for c in quals) / len(quals), printed with f"{mean:.1f}".
GC percentage: count("G") + count("C") over the total length of the kept reads, times 100.

checks.label: Reads are scored, filtered and summarised

realityNote: FastQC and fastp do this over millions of reads with per-position statistics and adapter trimming. A mean threshold of Q20 is a common first filter; variant calling later uses the per-base scores, not the mean.
